newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico interest rates appear at peak - Abaco.
newsitem.headline: Mexico interest rates appear at peak - Abaco.

text.p: Mexican interest rates appear to have peaked after climbing at the last two primary Cetes auctions, Casa de Bolsa Abaco said in a report released on Thursday.

The brokerage said interest rates have increased marginally as part of the aftershock from the Federal Reserve's move to boost U.S. rates last month and increased tightness in the money base in Mexico.
It said its outlook reflects a strengthening peso and strong demand for government securities, among other factors. At the same time, it recommended investing in 91-day and 181-day paper.
Abaco outlined its reasons as follows:

-- "Given expected inflation of 3.5 percent for the next three months, the 91-day forward rate is now close to 10 percent, which is on the high side given the stability of the peso, the level of reserves and the improvement in the economy."
-- "The effect of the U.S. rate hike on Mexico's external payments is only $40 million (U.S.). There is no reason for local Mexican rates to continue reacting to U.S. rate hikes."
-- "The demand for government securities continues to far outstrip supply, and foreign investors are aggressive buyers."
-- "We do not expect significant pressure on the peso in the short term, and, at most, would look for a two percent to three percent slippage by midyear."
The brokerage also said that concerns over the coming midterm elections in July appear to be easing gradually.
